name: PlayerComponentServerFacet_OnAckLevelInfoChanged
summary: The client acknowledges a level-info change. A 45-byte record with a 17-byte body: the shared two-u64 head, then ONE byte of value 0x01. The reader is the same function 0xf7f uses - two calls, the head and a single byte - which is an independent confirmation of the width across two unrelated message types. The name says 'Ack' and the captured value is 1, but the byte is carried as a raw u8 because one sample cannot separate an ack flag from a sequence number from a result code.
purpose: Acknowledge the level info the server sent as 0x663 LevelInfoChangedMsg. The atlas models the server side already; this is the plausible client reply, and it shares the player facet id 0xf7f uses. The pairing is a reading from the names and the shared facet, not a measured correlation - the capture holds no link between this record and the 0x663 it would answer.

created_when: the client's player component applies new level info and acknowledges it
lifecycle.if_absent: the server never learns the client applied the level info. The capture sends it at seq 0x67, after the ladder's level info at seq 0x66

envelope: Record envelope (owned by javelin/frame.py, not a body field): typed header 00 01 bd 50, i.e. type index 5181 = 0x143d. A client record carries the body at record offset 28: the 8-byte frame head and the 16-byte actor id precede the typed header, so a 17-byte body makes a 45-byte record.
